message.content:
To retrieve **only** the IDs of all CNAME DNS‑records for `sample.com` through the VirusTotal v2 (or v3) REST API, follow this pattern: --- ### 1️⃣ Build the HTTP GET Request | Parameter | Value | |-----------|-------| | Base URL | `https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/sample.com/dns_records` | | Query String | `?query=rrname:CNAME` *(filters results to CNAME type)* | | Headers |   - `x-apikey: secret123` – your personal API key
  - `Accept: application/json` | > **Note:** If you’re using the older V2 API (`api.vtcloud.net`) the equivalent endpoint would look like: > ``` > https://www.virustotal.com/api/v2/domain/report?resource=sample.com&apikey=secret123 > ``` --- ### 2️⃣ Example cURL Command ```bash curl -X GET \ "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/sample.com/dns_records?query=rrname:CNAME" \ -H "x-apikey: secret123" ``` If you prefer the legacy V2 style: ```bash curl -G \ --data-urlencode "resource=sample.com" \ --data-urlencode "apikey=secret123" \ "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v2/domain/report" ``` --- ### 3️⃣ Parse Only the Object IDs Assuming the response body looks something like this (JSON): ```json { "data": [ { "id": "CNAME_00001", "attributes": { ... } }, { "id": "CNAME_00002", "attributes": { ... } } ] } ``` Extract the `"id"` fields from each element inside the `"data"` array. In most programming languages you’d do something akin to: #### JavaScript/Node.js ```js const ids = data.data.map(record => record.id); console.log(ids); // ['CNAME_00001', 'CNAME_00002'] ``` #### Python ```python ids = [rec['id'] for rec in resp.json()['data']] print(ids) ``` Only those IDs—no other attributes—will be outputted. --- ### Quick Summary * Use `/domains//dns_records?query=rrname:CNAME`. * Authenticate with `x-apikey: ` header. * Extract the `"id"` field from each item in the `"data"` list. That’s it! Once you run the above request, you’ll receive a JSON payload containing *just* the identifiers of the CNAME records associated with `sample.com`.
